edges.description: Reduced P5CS function can alter proline- and ornithine-pathway output, but plasma amino-acid concentrations are not uniformly low across genotypes.
Dominant ALDH18A1 dysfunction produces pure or complex hereditary spastic paraplegia; the tissue-level bridge from P5CS dysfunction is unresolved.
Biallelic P5CS dysfunction can reduce pathway output, although molecularly confirmed patients can have normal plasma amino-acid concentrations.
Some biallelic variants cause complex SPG9B without cutaneous abnormality; the intervening neural tissue mechanism is unknown.
Cognitive impairment is reported in complex SPG9B but is not universal; the intervening neural mechanism is unknown.
Other biallelic ALDH18A1 variants cause ARCL3A; the tissue mechanisms separating this neurocutaneous branch from SPG9B remain unresolved.
In the homozygous p.Thr331Pro subgroup, impaired incorporation of P5CS monomers into oligomers accompanies measured fibroblast changes.
edges.target: p.Thr331Pro fibroblast metabolic and transcript changes

edges.description: In compound-heterozygous p.Arg749Gln/p.Arg765Gln fibroblasts, reduced P5CS stability co-occurs with a lipid-droplet phenotype; no clinical causal bridge is implied.
Homozygous p.Arg84Gln markedly reduces P5CS activity and defines the reported hyperammonemic, low-amino-acid branch rather than a universal biochemical profile.
Corticospinal involvement is expressed clinically as lower-limb spastic paraplegia in dominant and recessive SPG9.
Intellectual disability is a reported, non-universal manifestation of complex SPG9B.
ARCL3A includes global developmental delay; the intervening neural mechanism is unknown.

ARCL3A includes lax, wrinkled, or inelastic skin. The full tissue-level mechanism remains unresolved, though patient dermal fibroblasts show reduced type I/III collagen production and altered elastin ultrastructure, a partial extracellular-matrix explanation.
Joint laxity is part of ARCL3A, without a proven extracellular-matrix causal bridge.
The triangular, progeroid facial appearance is a defining clinical characteristic of the ARCL3A/de Barsy branch; its tissue-level mechanism remains unresolved.
Congenital hypotonia can occur in ARCL3A, although GeneReviews reports it at the grouped neurocutaneous-disorder level and the intervening mechanism is unknown.
Corneal clouding can occur in ARCL3A, but the grouped GeneReviews evidence does not establish its frequency or a direct corneal mechanism.
Cataracts are reported in ARCL3A, but the lens mechanism is unknown and is not attributed to the fibroblast lipid-droplet observation.
ARCL3A growth involvement includes short stature; its intermediate mechanism is unknown.
Microcephaly occurs in ARCL3A, with an unresolved developmental mechanism.
Visible superficial veins are reported in ARCL3A without a proven direct tissue mechanism.
Failure to thrive is reported in ARCL3A, while its intermediate mechanism is unresolved.
Severe speech delay accompanies developmental impairment in ARCL3A; the intervening neural mechanism is unknown.
Dystonic posturing is the discriminatory ALDH18A1/PYCR1 neurocutaneous movement sign; the route from P5CS dysfunction to the basal-ganglia/motor phenotype is unresolved.
Corpus callosum dysgenesis is a CNS malformation associated with ALDH18A1 defects; the developmental mechanism from P5CS dysfunction is unresolved.
Congenital hip dislocation is a connective-tissue/skeletal feature of the ALDH18A1-related neurocutaneous group; the extracellular-matrix bridge is not established.
Adducted thumbs are among the skeletal/positional features of the ALDH18A1-related neurocutaneous group; the mechanistic bridge is unknown.
In the p.Arg84Gln sibling pair, the genotype-specific metabolic branch manifested as hyperammonemia.
Low plasma proline supports impaired P5CS-dependent amino-acid synthesis, while a normal result does not exclude it.
Low plasma ornithine supports impaired P5CS-dependent amino-acid synthesis, while a normal result does not exclude it.
Low plasma citrulline supports impaired P5CS-dependent amino-acid synthesis, while a normal result does not exclude it.
Low plasma arginine supports impaired P5CS-dependent amino-acid synthesis, while a normal result does not exclude it.
Elevated ammonia reports the p.Arg84Gln-associated metabolic branch rather than the full ALDH18A1 spectrum.
Lower cellular glutathione reports the p.Thr331Pro fibroblast metabolic phenotype and is not generalized to every ALDH18A1 variant.
